clearanceData.description: Starting knife clearance ranges by material and thickness, and burr height limits by end use. All values are recommended reference values; confirm by test slitting.
clearanceData.datasetDescription: Recommended single-side knife clearance for metal slitting by material (mild steel, stainless steel, aluminum, copper and brass) and thickness, with adjustment rules for high-strength steel, galvanized steel and silicon steel, plus burr height limits by end use. Compiled by TOA DR Enterprise; confirm settings by test slitting.

calculator.outOfRange: The data table has no value for this thickness. It covers {min}–{max} mm for this material.
calculator.basis: Based on the row for {min}–{max} mm in the clearance data table.
calculator.disclaimer: A starting point only. The right clearance also depends on the machine, the knife condition and the material batch.

data.heading: Slitting Clearance Data Table
data.intro: These are the starting clearance ranges used across slitter.ai, including the calculator. Clearance is the horizontal gap between the upper and lower knife, on a single side (at each cut), as a percentage of material thickness, not the total of both sides.
data.reference: Reference values: use them as a starting point and confirm by test slitting.
data.burrIntro: Common burr height limits by end use, as a percentage of material thickness. The customer's specification always takes precedence.
